claims.title: Charter of Ban Kulin
claims.summary: Ban Kulin granted the merchants of Dubrovnik (Ragusa) freedom to trade across Bosnia; the document is one of the oldest state charters of the South Slavs and a landmark of early Bosnian statehood.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1189-charter-of-ban-kulin, claim TL:BIH:event:1189:charter-of-ban-kulin, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Stjepan Kotromanić expands Bosnia
claims.summary: Ban Stjepan Kotromanić of the Kotromanić dynasty enlarged Bosnia southward, incorporating the principality of Hum, the territory later known as Herzegovina.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1322-stjepan-kotromanic-expands-bosnia, claim TL:BIH:event:1322:stjepan-kotromanic-expands-bosnia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coronation of Tvrtko I
claims.summary: Tvrtko I was crowned king, raising Bosnia from a banate to a kingdom; under him it reached the Dalmatian coast and became, briefly, the most powerful state in the western Balkans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1377-coronation-of-tvrtko-i, claim TL:BIH:event:1377:coronation-of-tvrtko-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The stećci tombstones
claims.summary: Across medieval Bosnia, communities raised monumental carved limestone tombstones known as stećci; sites in Bosnia and neighbouring lands were inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 2016.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1450-the-stecci-tombstones, claim TL:BIH:event:1450:the-stecci-tombstones, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Bosnia
claims.summary: The armies of Sultan Mehmed II conquered most of Bosnia in 1463, ending the medieval kingdom and beginning more than four centuries of Ottoman rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1463-ottoman-conquest-of-bosnia, claim TL:BIH:event:1463:ottoman-conquest-of-bosnia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bosnia incorporated into the Ottoman Empire
claims.summary: Following the conquest, Bosnia became an Ottoman province; the settlement of Vrhbosna was developed into Sarajevo, the future provincial capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1463-bosnia-incorporated-into-the-ottoman-empire, claim TL:BIH:event:1463:bosnia-incorporated-into-the-ottoman-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Islamization and a multi-confessional society
claims.summary: Over generations much of Bosnia's Slavic population converted to Islam, creating, alongside Orthodox, Catholic and Jewish communities, the uniquely interwoven multi-confessional society that defines the country.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1550-islamization-and-a-multi-confessional-society, claim TL:BIH:event:1550:islamization-and-a-multi-confessional-society, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge, Višegrad
claims.summary: The eleven-arch Ottoman bridge over the Drina at Višegrad was built to designs by the imperial architect Sinan; it was inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage in 2007.

sources.label: Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge in Višegrad (inscribed 2007)

claims.title: The Old Bridge at Mostar (Stari Most)
claims.summary: The single-arch Old Bridge over the Neretva, a masterpiece of Ottoman engineering, gave Mostar its name; the Old City of Mostar was inscribed by UNESCO in 2005 after the bridge's wartime destruction and reconstruction.

sources.label: Old Bridge Area of the Old City of Mostar (inscribed 2005)

claims.title: Herzegovinian uprising and the Eastern Crisis
claims.summary: A peasant revolt in Herzegovina widened into a great-power crisis over the 'Eastern Question', ending Ottoman rule and leading to Austro-Hungarian occupation in 1878.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1875-herzegovinian-uprising-and-the-eastern-crisis, claim TL:BIH:event:1875:herzegovinian-uprising-and-the-eastern-crisis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Austro-Hungarian occupation
claims.summary: The Congress of Berlin authorised Austria-Hungary to occupy and administer Bosnia and Herzegovina, ending effective Ottoman rule while leaving nominal sovereignty in Istanbul.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1878-austro-hungarian-occupation, claim TL:BIH:event:1878:austro-hungarian-occupation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annexation by Austria-Hungary
claims.summary: Vienna formally annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina, triggering a European diplomatic crisis and inflaming South Slav nationalist opposition to Habsburg rule.

sources.label: Archduke Franz Ferdinand
sources.publisher: Lumen Learning, History of Western Civilization II

claims.title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
claims.summary: In Sarajevo, Gavrilo Princip of the Young Bosnia movement shot dead Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie, the act that triggered the outbreak of the First World War.

sources.label: Archduke Franz Ferdinand
sources.publisher: Lumen Learning, History of Western Civilization II

claims.title: Bosnia joins the Yugoslav kingdom
claims.summary: With Austria-Hungary's collapse, Bosnia was incorporated into the new Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later renamed Yugoslavia, losing its separate administrative identity.

claims.title: Axis invasion and the NDH
claims.summary: The Axis dismembered Yugoslavia and incorporated Bosnia into the Ustaša-led Independent State of Croatia, whose terror against Serbs, Jews and Roma helped ignite a brutal multi-sided civil war.

sources.label: World War II and the establishment of ZAVNOBiH

claims.title: First session of ZAVNOBiH
claims.summary: At Mrkonjić Grad the anti-fascist council ZAVNOBiH proclaimed Bosnia and Herzegovina a federal unit of its equal peoples, ensuring it would be restored as a distinct republic within Yugoslavia.

sources.label: World War II and the establishment of ZAVNOBiH

claims.title: Bosnia a republic of socialist Yugoslavia
claims.summary: After the Partisan victory, Bosnia and Herzegovina became one of the six federal republics of Tito's socialist Yugoslavia, with its multi-ethnic society constitutionally recognised.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1945-bosnia-a-republic-of-socialist-yugoslavia, claim TL:BIH:event:1945:bosnia-a-republic-of-socialist-yugoslavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sarajevo Winter Olympics
claims.summary: Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympic Games, a high point of confidence for the multi-ethnic socialist republic less than a decade before war engulfed the city.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Bosnia and Herzegovina: A medieval kingdom turned Ottoman, Habsburg and Yugoslav crossroads, scarred by the 1990s war yet remade as a single multi-ethnic state.", terralore.co/country/BIH/chronicle#ev-1984-sarajevo-winter-olympics, claim TL:BIH:event:1984:sarajevo-winter-olympics, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence referendum
claims.summary: Bosnians voted overwhelmingly for independence in a referendum largely boycotted by Serbs; the country was recognised internationally and joined the UN on 22 May 1992.

sources.label: The Breakup of Yugoslavia, 1990–1992
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Siege of Sarajevo begins
claims.summary: Bosnian Serb forces encircled and shelled the capital from the surrounding hills; lasting about 1,425 days, it became the longest siege of a capital city in modern history.

claims.title: Ethnic cleansing and the Bosnian War
claims.summary: Campaigns to expel and destroy rival communities through killings, deportation, detention camps and sexual violence devastated Bosnia, crimes later prosecuted before the ICTY.

sources.label: The Breakup of Yugoslavia, 1990–1992
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: The Srebrenica genocide
claims.summary: After overrunning the UN 'safe area', Bosnian Serb forces under Ratko Mladić executed up to 8,000 Bosniak men and boys; the ICTY and ICJ ruled the killings genocide.

claims.title: Dayton Agreement initialled
claims.summary: After negotiations led by Richard Holbrooke, the General Framework Agreement for Peace was initialled at Dayton, Ohio, ending the Bosnian War.

claims.title: Dayton Agreement signed in Paris
claims.summary: The peace agreement was formally signed in Paris, preserving a single Bosnian state divided into two entities, the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, with an Office of the High Representative.

sources.label: The Dayton Peace Agreement (General Framework Agreement for Peace)

claims.summary: Binding arbitration under Annex 2 created the Brčko District, a self-governing unit held in condominium by both entities under the sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
